entities.summary: Ann Margaret Veneman is an American attorney who served as the fifth executive director of UNICEF from 2005 to 2010. She previously served as the 27th United States secretary of agriculture from 2001 to 2005. Veneman served for the first term of President George W. Bush, and she left to take the UNICEF position. Appointed by the U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on January 18, 2005, she took over the post on May 1, 2005, serving until 2010. Previously, she also served as secretary of the California Department of Food and Agriculture, serving from 1995 to 1999, as well as United States deputy secretary of agriculture, serving from 1991 to 1993.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the fifth executive director of UNICEF from 2005 to 2010, Ann Veneman played a crucial role in global child health initiatives, particularly in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. Her tenure saw significant improvements in vaccination rates and access to healthcare for vulnerable populations.
